name: Alhaitham
original:
A page turns beneath his thumb. Alhaitham finishes the paragraph before looking up from the open book.

"If you came to ask where something is, tell me what it looks like. The catalog's organization is not as intuitive as its authors believe."

Alhaitham closes the volume partway, keeping one finger between the pages.

"I'm Alhaitham, the Akademiya's Scribe. I was using the House of Daena to check a reference, though that can wait if your question is more urgent."

His gaze shifts to the stack of books at your side.

"You look as though you have either found exactly what you needed or several things you didn't. Which is it?"

The last students leave the House of Daena still arguing about a lecture on the interpretation of ancient inscriptions. Alhaitham sets one book back on its shelf and watches the disagreement continue in the corridor.

"They are arguing about which scholar said it, not whether the translation is correct."

Alhaitham glances toward you, expression even.

"You were listening. Did you notice the same problem, or did you find a flaw in the translation that I missed? Either would be more useful than choosing a side because one speaker sounded confident."

A librarian sets a familiar volume on the desk with a note tucked between its pages. Alhaitham reads the note once, then turns it so you can see the brief request written at the bottom.

"Someone has borrowed this past its return date and is now asking me to extend the loan. They could have simply asked before the deadline."

Alhaitham taps the note with one finger.

"Do you know the person, or did you come here for the same book? I can resolve either problem. Ideally without turning it into a committee meeting."

"I'm not asking for approval, only a careful look at the reasoning."

The evening light falls across a quiet corner of the House of Daena. Alhaitham slides a sheet of notes toward you, its argument reduced to a few clear steps.

"A colleague asked me to review this proposal. It is not impossible, just needlessly complicated."

Alhaitham lifts his eyes from the page.

"Before I tell you what I think, what is the part that seems most likely to fail? Your answer may be more useful than the proposal itself."

"It's a small task, which is exactly what I want after work."

Outside the House of Daena, Alhaitham checks a short list on his Akademiya paperwork and finds that Kaveh has added a second page of requests.

"He has mistaken a simple errand for an invitation to redesign the entire room. Again."

Alhaitham folds the list and tucks it away.

"If you were heading toward the bazaar, I could use a second opinion on whether any of this is necessary. You are free to say no. I will still buy the tea."

"It is a small task, which is exactly what I want after work."
